course_description:
This course provides students with techniques for evaluating investments on an individual basis and in the context of portfolio theory and asset pricing. Techniques for analysing investments focus on maximising expected returns while minimising risk are covered. Fixed income security analysis and fund performance are detailed.

This course covers the two main types of investments - equity and debt investments - along with a week on alternative investments and a week on ethics and standards. Our objective is to develop skills in pricing financial assets and forming portfolios which maximise expected return for a given level of risk.

Course Changes in Response to Previous Student Feedback

In response to student feedback, we are introducing a portfolio simulation component into the assessment.

course_aims: This course provides students with techniques for pricing financial investments on an individual basis and evaluating in the context of a portfolio. Techniques for analysing portfolio investments focus on maximising expected returns while minimising risk. Therefore, students should achieve the ability to value investments and quantify the contribution they make to the risk of a portfolio. Students will also learn the role of ethics and professional standards within the investment management process.

learning_outcomes.description: Understand factors that impact financial markets.
Analyse financial data in order to assess a particular investment or investment strategy.
Perform and evaluate different techniques to value equity, debt, and alternative investments.
Explain and evaluate the risks associated with investing, including understanding ethical and professional standards in an investment management context.
Analyse techniques for portfolio creation and to measure portfolio performance.

assessment_details.task_description: This assessment consists of two integrated components. As a group of 5–6 students , members will jointly select a number of equities equal to the group size and use these stocks to construct and actively manage a AUD 10,000 simulated investment portfolio , evaluating its performance and risk relative to a benchmark. For benchmarking purposes, use the ISHARES CORE S&P/ASX 200 ETF (replicating ASX 200) as the benchmark portfolio. Individually , each student will conduct a discounted cash flow (DCF) valuation of one non-financial service company that is included in the group’s portfolio and provide a justified investment recommendation. This assessment evaluates students’ collaborative portfolio management skills as well as their individual ability to apply valuation techniques and assess investment decisions in a real-world investment context. In writing your Investment Policy Statement (IPS), Your individual equity valuation report is no more than 2 pages and typed in 12pt Times New Roman with 1.5 line spacing and normal margin. Your group portfolio simulation report is no more than 2,500 words with 10% allowance and typed in 12pt Times New Roman with 1.5 line spacing and normal margin.
